claims.summary: For a smooth projective geometrically integral curve X/k of genus g, divisor A and effective divisor E of degree e, deg A>=e+g gives a nonzero f in L(A-E). If a k-rational P avoids supports of A,E and deg A>=e+2g, one can choose f(P)=1. Standard Riemann-Roch and point-evaluation consequence: vanishing along E is as an O(A) section, and as a rational function when A/E supports are disjoint. Separate protected-value budget; no PC curve model or optimality assertion.
claims.assessment: Working standard consequence of primary Riemann-Roch and negative-degree section statements, passed by the sole medium reviewer and section/function correction check; not a new curve theorem.
claims.rationale: A geometric quantitative provider for common locators whose degree and protected value are independently controlled by defect length and genus.
claims.next_action: Develop a concrete geometric repair application with exact representation and construction costs.

claims.summary: For every n>=3 over F2 in the Boolean-only degree4 quotient, U the multilinear degree<=2 domain, g=(x1,x2), and any q in span g, the error map f->((1+q)x1 f,(1+q)x2 f) cannot be represented with the same left kernel by one scalar native rectangle mu(E f h), E a scalar error combination and full right degree<=L at deg E+2+L<=4. For q nonzero the actual rank>=2 while L=0 gives rank<=1; for q=0 actual rank=n(n+1)/2>n+1 while L<=1. This is not an obstruction to arbitrary native forms or several functionals. Separately R=k[t],I=(t),M=R,N=(t^m) has exact Artin-Rees delay m; the m-state shift with first-coordinate observation needs m observations to reach zero common kernel. The latter controls hold over every field and m>=1.
claims.assessment: Working symbolic scope controls passed by the sole medium reviewer: a narrow native-rectangle obstruction and standard sharp stabilization examples. They do not refute multiplier existence or provide a new selection bound.
claims.rationale: Tests stronger conveniences introduced by candidate bridges at their actual costs, distinguishing a finite representation or stabilization theorem from an affordable repair.
